title: Development of a Low-Cost Light-weight Milk Chilling Can for Small-Scale Dairy Farmers
org: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
dataset_link: Dairy temperature monitoring and milk quality datasets collected from local dairy cooperatives or experimental field trials.
description:
• Background Milk is a highly perishable agricultural product that begins to deteriorate rapidly after milking due to bacterial growth and enzymatic activity. ln many rural and remote dairy-producing regions, particularly Hilly and North Eastern Regions, farmers lack access to bulk milk cooling facilities and reliable electricity. As a result, milk often remains at ambient temperatures for several hours before reaching collection centers, leading to quality degradation, reduced shelf life and economic losses. Available solutions are expensive, relatively heavy and low volume storage cans, making them uneconomical for use or during transportation.
• Description The proposed problem aims to develop a low-cost, lightweight milk chilling can capable of maintaining milk at safe storage temperatures during collection and transportation. The can should be manufactured using food-grade lightweight materials such as High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE), aluminum alloys or composite materials while ensuring structural strength and hygiene standards.The design should incorporate an insulated double-wall structure with materials such as polyurethane foam (PUF) or other cost-effective insulating materials to minimize heat transfer.
The chilling mechanism may utilize reusable ice packs, phase change materials (PCM), or passive cooling technologies that do not require continuous electrical power. The system should be capable of maintaining milk temperatures between 4°C and 8°C for several hours under typical rural environmental conditions.The solution should also consider ease of handling, cleaning, transportation and durability.Optional features such as a temperature monitoring indicator, leak-proof lid and ergonomic handles may be included to improve usability. The product should be affordable enough for adoption by small and marginal dairy farmers and suitable for village-level milk collection systems/centres.
• Expected Solution A lightweight, insulated milk chilling can with a capacity of 30-40 litres that can maintain milk at safe temperatures for at least 6-12 hours without external power supply. The developed solution should reduce milk spoilage, improve milk quality during transportation, lower handling effort due lo reduced weight and cost significantly less than conventional insulated stainless-steel chilling containers. The final prototype should be durable, food-safe, easy to manufacture and suitable for widespread deployment in rural dairy supply chains.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a agriculture, foodtech & rural development problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development. Tech Depth (1/5): centers on moderate engineering scope. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Development of a Low-Cost Light-weight Milk Chilling Can for Small-Scale Dairy Farmers

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a lightweight, affordable insulated milk can that keeps milk at safe temperatures during collection and transport in remote areas without electricity, replacing the heavy, expensive cans that make this genuinely hard for small farmers.
overview.why_it_matters: Milk quality degrades fast without cooling, and remote farmers without electricity currently have no affordable option. A genuinely lighter, cheaper can directly protects farmer income from spoilage losses.
pain_points: Farmers in hilly/remote regions lack access to bulk cooling and reliable electricity.
Milk sits at ambient temperature for hours, degrading quality and shelf life.
Existing cooling cans are expensive, heavy, and low-volume, making them impractical.
overview.background: Milk quality degrades rapidly without cooling, and remote, electricity-scarce regions lack affordable, lightweight cooling solutions for collection and transport, current options are too expensive and heavy.
overview.whats_being_asked: A low-cost, lightweight, insulated milk chilling can maintaining safe storage temperatures during collection and transportation, using food-grade lightweight materials.
expected_solution: Lightweight, food-grade can construction (HDPE, aluminum alloy, or composite).

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental. Insulated container design is well-established engineering, the innovation is in optimizing specifically for low weight and low cost while maintaining hygiene and thermal performance.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Very low. Straightforward materials and insulation engineering, achievable with basic fabrication access.

competitive_landscape.note: Simple, accessible hardware PS draws fewer software-first teams, genuinely achievable low-competition lane for a hardware-capable team.

innovation.note: Established insulated-container engineering, applied to a specific cost/weight optimization target.

invention.note: Straightforward materials and construction, minimal technical complexity.

technical_feasibility.note: Achievable with basic materials and fabrication access, no exotic components needed.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly reduces spoilage losses for remote small-scale dairy farmers, concrete, measurable income protection.

architecture.note: A single physical container, no complex system integration.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, similar profile to other hardware-livelihood PS in this batch, genuinely achievable and impactful for a hardware-capable team, low innovation ceiling but real, provable value.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Fully achievable end-to-end physical demo in 36 hours with accessible materials, low technical risk.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A team without materials/fabrication access or comfort will struggle to have a working physical prototype.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm access to basic lightweight materials (HDPE sheet, aluminum, PUF insulation) and basic fabrication tools before committing.

idea_0_4: Scope to a smaller-scale demo can, not a full commercial-size unit.
Choose your material combination (HDPE outer, PUF insulation is a reasonable, accessible choice) and source materials.
Split: one person on the can construction, one on insulation and testing.
prototype_4_22: Build the double-wall insulated can structure.
Start temperature-retention testing with real milk or a water proxy.
integration_22_30: Test actual temperature retention over time compared to an uninsulated control.
Measure the can's actual weight versus existing heavy cans.
Refine insulation/construction based on test results.
polish_30_36: Prepare your real measured temperature-retention and weight-comparison data as your key evidence.
Build a simple cost breakdown for your prototype.
Rehearse leading with the farmer income-protection story before showing the physical unit.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show real logged temperature data from your can versus an uninsulated control over the test period, and its actual weight compared to existing heavy cans, real measured numbers make the value proposition concrete.

strengths: Fully achievable, low technical risk within 36 hours.
Concrete, measurable value proposition (temperature retention, weight, cost).
weaknesses: Requires real materials and basic fabrication access.
Low innovation ceiling, differentiation depends on execution quality (actual measured performance).

team_fit.approach: Source materials in hour 0, this is the actual bottleneck for a hardware PS like this.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The cost-analysis writeup and any temperature-logging data visualization.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly sizing insulation thickness and material choice for real thermal performance, that's applied materials/thermal engineering.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-suggested material spec without real physical testing risks under-performing on actual thermal retention, physical validation is unavoidable here.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, resourcing risk is physical materials access.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If full materials aren't available, demo with substitute accessible materials while being clear about the intended final material choice and its expected performance difference.

judge_qna.question: What's your actual measured temperature retention, not the theoretical target?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your logged temperature data over your test period compared to an uninsulated control, real numbers.
judge_qna.follow_up: How does performance change with ambient temperature or longer transport durations?

judge_qna.question: How does the actual weight and cost compare to existing cans on the market?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your real measured weight and cost breakdown directly against known existing product specifications.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the durability tradeoff of using lighter materials versus traditional heavier cans?
